maya: Quick heads-up — I ran the nightly mixed-quant perf+eval on model-prod-3 (fp8 + 4-bit kernels with int8 fallback). Throughput looks better (~+18% tokens/sec) but we have a worrying delta on structured outputs and hallucination score. Posting raw snippets so we can triage. @sam @jordan :eyes:

perf-bot: perf-run complete — id=pr-17951, commit=3f7a2b, avg_p95_latency=210ms (+12ms), tokens/s=1220 (+18%), eval_report=/artifacts/pr-17951/report.json :white_check_mark:

maya: Eval deltas (baseline float32 -> mixed-quant):
```
metric                        baseline   quantized   delta
structured_parse_f1           92.3       86.1        -6.2
exact_match                   98.1       95.7        -2.4
hallucination_rate            0.8%       2.7%        +1.9pp
json_schema_valid            99.4%      93.8%       -5.6pp
```

maya: Notable: structured_parse_f1 and json_schema_valid drop the most — suggests the model is producing syntactically valid but semantically wrong structure or tokenization shifts breaking deterministic parsers.

sam: Huh. Which kernels did runtime pick? Any fallback events logged? :thinking:

maya: Runtime logs show kernel selection sequence: prefer_fp8 -> prefer_4bit_fast -> int8_fallback. We saw a handful of fallbacks around KV population for seq_len>256. Snippet from runtime trace: 
```
[2026-11-12T02:34:10Z] kernel_select: chosen=matmul_fp8_v3 (weight_q=fp8)
[2026-11-12T02:34:11Z] kernel_fallback: reason=kv_pad_align mismatch -> chosen=matmul_4bit_fast
[2026-11-12T02:34:12Z] kernel_fallback: reason=accum_precision limit -> chosen=matmul_int8_v2
```

jordan: Those fallback transitions during KV population are suspicious. If the KV cache stores mixed-precision caches and we later reuse them with a different kernel path, rounding / dequant differences could accumulate and corrupt structured outputs.

ryan: Yep — I've seen similar before. Batching heuristic grouped a short-context user with a long-context system prompt in the same batch; KV cache write used caller's kernel tag but subsequent reads used fallback kernel tag mismatch. We need per-request KV metadata to avoid merging incompatible caches.

maya: Do we currently tag KV entries with kernel/quant meta? I thought we only tag by model_version + shape.

sam: Right now tags = {model:v, seq_len_bucket, device_shard}. No kernel precision tag. That means identical shape + version but different quant path will share a slot. :bug:

ling: Proposed quick mitigations:
- Add kernel_precision tag on KV key (cheap, fixes mixing).
- Re-run calibration with per-channel scales for fp8/4bit (we currently use per-tensor for speed).
- Change batching heuristic to avoid mixing short vs long contexts when kernel policy toggles.

sam: Agreed. Also calibration: we've been using a 128-sample global calibration set. For structured outputs we should run localized calibration on the structured parsing dataset and produce per-channel scales. Per-channel reduces quant noise but increases storage of scales.

jordan: I can reproduce a small case locally if someone points me at the model checkpoint + runtime flags. I suspect matmul_int8_v2 has a different accumulation path that perturbs repeated KV reads.

maya: Repro steps I used:
```
# runner snippet
runtimeserve --model model-prod-3 --kernel-policy "fp8_then_4bit_then_int8" \
  --batching.max_batch=64 --batching.short_cutoff=128 --kv.enabled=true --kv.shard=true
# eval harness
python eval/structured_parsing_v2.py --dataset samples/structured_1000.jsonl --out out/pr-17951.json
```

ryan: Short-term hotfix we can deploy without kernel work: force kernel_policy to 'fp8_strict' (reject fallbacks) for the canary cluster and force kv tag by adding kernel_precision to key. That will reduce throughput but let us confirm whether mixing is root cause.

maya: Can we test these permutations? Ling — can you schedule matrix? Something like:
A) float32 baseline
B) fp8-only (no fallback)
C) fp8+4bit mixed (current)
D) fp8+4bit + kv:kernel_tag (new)
E) fp8+4bit + per-channel calibration
F) fp8+4bit + disable_kv_cache

ling: Will do. Scheduling now. perf-bot, please queue jobs: pr-17951-A..F on model-prod-3 small-canaary. Use eval set structured_parsing_v2. :calendar: 

perf-bot: jobs queued: pr-17951-A..F (6 runs). Estimated finish ~25m. Notifying #eng-runtime when done. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

sam: If A vs B shows no structure regression but C does -> mixing or 4bit kernel is culprit. If D fixes it, it's definitely KV mixing. If E reduces delta but not D, then calibration was partial.

jordan: For the kernel team, here's a minimal change to avoid accumulation mismatch: add a fast-path that converts cached KV into the caller kernel precision on read using per-channel scaling if available. Pseudocode: 
```
if cache.precision != caller.precision:
  if cache.has_per_channel_scales:
    dequantise_per_channel(cache)  # convert to float
    requantise_per_channel(cache, caller.precision)
  else:
    invalidate_cache_entry()
```

maya: Good plan. I'll start by running the scheduled matrix and post the artifacts. Assigning followups: @sam for kernel tagging + config, @jordan for reproducer + kernel fallback trace, @ryan for batching tweak, @ling to collect eval outputs. I'll collect results and open a follow-up incident ticket if any run shows json_schema_valid < 95%. :mag:

sam: I'll prioritize a KV key change (kernel_precision tag) and push a small runtime flag `kv.include_precision=true` on a staging branch. Expect PR in ~2h. :hammer_and_wrench: :thumbsup:

ling: perf runs queued, will post summary when they land.

maya: Thanks everyone. If perf-bot finishes early ping me — I'll start looking at the worst failing examples to see whether it's a tokenizer shift or true semantic failure. :fire:

perf-bot: job pr-17951-B finished (fp8-only) — report=/artifacts/pr-17951-B/report.json, structured_parse_f1=91.8, json_schema_valid=96.9

maya: Nice, fp8-only looks much closer to baseline. That points at mixed pipeline (4bit or int8 fallbacks or KV mixing) being the main issue.

sam: Ok locking on the KV-tag change as first action. Will post PR link when ready.

maya: Closing loop — I'll collect sample failures and create an eval diff doc for the kernel team. Closing this thread after results. :white_check_mark:
